source_construct: set confusion_matrix_train end=eof + retain TP TN FP FN 0 + keep train_precision train_recall train_f1_score train_accuracy
target_translation: one explicit aggregation, one output row (RULEBOOK retain/end=eof row). cm = confusion_matrix_train (PROC FREQ out=: one row per OBSERVED (default_flag, pred_logistic) cell, count column COUNT). TP, TN, FP, FN = cm.filter((pl.col('default_flag') == d) & (pl.col('pred_logistic') == p))['COUNT'].sum() for (1,1), (0,0), (0,1), (1,0): a cell PROC FREQ does not output is never assigned, so it keeps the retain initial value 0, and polars' sum of an empty selection is also 0. Then once (the if-eof block; the explicit OUTPUT suppresses the implicit per-row output): train_precision = TP/(TP+FP) if TP+FP > 0 else None; train_recall = TP/(TP+FN) if TP+FN > 0 else None; train_f1_score = 2*p*r/(p+r) if p is not None and r is not None and p+r > 0 else None (SAS: missing + x is missing and missing > 0 is false, so a missing precision or recall gives a missing f1); train_accuracy = (TP+TN)/(TP+TN+FP+FN) if that total > 0 else None. training_metrics = pl.DataFrame([[train_precision, train_recall, train_f1_score, train_accuracy]], schema={each: pl.Float64}, orient='row'): exactly 1 row; columns in first-assignment order (:128,:130,:132,:134), which keep preserves; TP..FN and the PROC FREQ columns are dropped. The counts are Python ints, so the guards are plain comparisons. A 0-row input would give 0 rows (unreachable: 105,000 training rows)
